This vignette describes how to add a model of aquatic mosquito ecology to
[`ramp.library`](https://github.com/dd-harp/ramp.library). Read the
[`ramp.xds` L interface vignette](https://dd-harp.github.io/ramp.xds/articles/L-interface.html)
first for an overview of how L modules connect to egg laying and emergence.
Before adding a module, check whether the model is already available in the
SimBA library.

An L module describes aquatic mosquito states in larval habitats. Its
methods operate on the habitat dimension, `nHabitats`, and use `s` as the
vector-species index. The habitat-to-patch `membership` vector is provided
when the module is set up.

## Creating a module template

The code chunks below can be extracted to create a starting R file. From
the directory containing this vignette, run:

```{r, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
knitr::purl(
  "L-How_To_Add_Model.Rmd",
  output = "Lmodule-newLname.R",
  documentation = 0,
  quiet = TRUE
)
```

The resulting file contains code examples that must be adapted before the
module is used. Replace `newLname` with a short, model-specific name. When
rendered, the chunks define the example functions but do not call them.

## General conventions

- Implement model methods as S3 methods named with the module class, such
  as `dLdt.newLname`.
- Use `s` to access the module at `xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]`.
- Store state indices in `xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$ix`, with one index per
  habitat for each habitat-level state.
- Keep state variables, derivatives, and discrete updates in the same
  order.
- Document model equations, states, parameters, inputs, outputs, and
  references with roxygen.
- Add tests for the module's equations, dimensions, and setup behavior.

### Documentation policy

Follow the shared [function order](https://dd-harp.github.io/ramp.xds/articles/XH-interface.html#function-order)
in module files and guide implementation sections. Move functions with their
documentation, keep file-level review/TODO notes at the top, and preserve
definitions and behavior when reordering.

Follow the shared [documentation conventions](https://dd-harp.github.io/ramp.xds/articles/XH-interface.html#documentation-conventions)
and the [L setup wording](https://dd-harp.github.io/ramp.xds/articles/L-interface.html#setup-documentation).
These vignettes are the public style reference for both packages.

- Use the approved family titles with a backticked module name and the
  **L** tag, including "Compute the derivatives for `module` (**L**)",
  "Mosquito bionomics for `module` (**L**)", and
  "Apply effect sizes for `module` (**L**)".
- Show the equations actually implemented, matching the returned state
  order. Describe derivative and updating equations separately, including
  any accessory variables and branches.
- Keep storage, class assignments, and dispatch mechanics in `@note`.
  Explain dispatch on the generic, not repeatedly on each method.
- List setup actions in implementation order: construction using
  `nHabitats` and `options`, skill set, initial values, habitat search
  weights, and return of the updated **`xds`** model object.
- Describe the habitat step as "Initialize habitat search weights using
  `[ramp.xds::setup_habitat_search_weights.setup]`." End complete bullets
  with periods and qualify links to shared helpers with `ramp.xds::`.
- Describe the skill set as capabilities and compatibilities. Include
  `dts = FALSE` if no discrete-time update method is defined; only advertise
  supported and tested solver pathways.
- State when a check method returns the model unchanged without checks.

Both dynamics methods below are placeholders. Keep the methods required
by the new module, replace the equations and their documentation together,
and update the skill set accordingly.

## Module dynamics

Implement `dLdt.newLname` for a continuous-time model, or
`Update_Lt.newLname` for a discrete-time model. Both receive time `t`, the
dependent-variable vector `y`, the **`xds`** model object, and the species
index `s`. A continuous-time method returns derivatives; a discrete-time
method returns updated states. They are alternative solver interfaces, not
interchangeable equations.

The habitat-level egg input is available as
`xds_obj$terms$eta[[s]]`. Extract the module states with `get_L_vars` and
use the indices and parameter values stored on the module object.

Retain "Compute the derivatives for `module` (**L**)" as the method title.
Begin descriptions "Compute the derivatives for the `module` module:"
and show the equations immediately below. Inherit the module NULL anchor's
state, input-term, parameter, and ODE or Dynamics sections. Use the actual
section names for existing modules; basicL uses `Dynamical Term` and stages
uses `Egg Laying` for its input. Document returned block order and length,
with each habitat-level block in habitat order. Keep dispatch on the shared
generic and storage details in `@note`.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Compute the derivatives for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Compute the derivatives for the `newLname` module:
#' \deqn{dL/dt = 0}
#' Replace this equation and the derivative code together.
#' @inheritSection newLname State Variables
#' @inheritSection newLname Dynamical Terms
#' @inheritSection newLname Parameters
#' @inheritSection newLname ODE
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::dLdt
#' @note Derivatives for `L` are returned in habitat order.
#' The egg input is read from `xds_obj$terms$eta[[s]]`.
#' @return a [numeric] vector of derivatives in the module's state-variable
#' order, with length `nHabitats`
#' @export
dLdt.newLname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  eta <- xds_obj$terms$eta[[s]]

  with(ramp.xds::get_L_vars(y, xds_obj, s), {
    with(xds_obj$L_obj[[s]], {
      # Replace this expression with the model's derivative equation.
      dL <- rep(0, xds_obj$nHabitats)
      derivatives <- c(dL)
      return(derivatives)
    })
  })
}
```

If the model has multiple states, extract each state in
`get_L_vars.newLname`, compute each derivative here, and concatenate them in
the same order used by `setup_L_ix.newLname`.

The discrete-time method has the same arguments and returns updated states
in that order. Write the model's discrete update equations directly; do not
substitute the continuous-time derivative or an Euler step unless that is
the model being implemented.

Use "Update states for `module` (**L**)" for the title and
"Update the state variables for the `module` module:" for the description,
followed by the updating equations in `\deqn{}`. Inherit the same NULL-anchor
sections as the derivative method, with `DTS` replacing `ODE`.
Document habitat ordering, return length, and egg-input storage as below.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Update states for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Update the state variables for the `newLname` module:
#' \deqn{L_{t+1} = 0}
#' Replace this equation and the updating code together.
#' @inheritSection newLname State Variables
#' @inheritSection newLname Dynamical Terms
#' @inheritSection newLname Parameters
#' @inheritSection newLname DTS
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::Update_Lt
#' @note Updated values for `L` are returned in habitat order.
#' The egg input is read from `xds_obj$terms$eta[[s]]`.
#' @return a [numeric] vector of updated states in the module's state-variable
#' order, with length `nHabitats`
#' @export
Update_Lt.newLname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  eta <- xds_obj$terms$eta[[s]]

  with(ramp.xds::get_L_vars(y, xds_obj, s), {
    with(xds_obj$L_obj[[s]], {
      # Replace this expression with the model's discrete update.
      Lt <- rep(0, xds_obj$nHabitats)
      states <- c(Lt)
      return(states)
    })
  })
}
```

## State-variable extraction

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Get the state variables for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Extract the state variables for the `newLname` module
#' from `y` and return them by name in a list for use during model solving.
#' @note Variable indices are stored at `xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$ix`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_L_vars
#' @return a named [list] of state variables and module-specific derived quantities
#' @export
get_L_vars.newLname <- function(y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$ix, {
    L <- y[L_ix]
    return(list(L = L))
  })
}
```

If the module has more than one state variable, create an index range for
each one and include each named state in the returned list.

## Bionomics and effect sizes

`LBionomics.newLname` updates baseline parameter values at time `t` and
resets effect sizes. `LEffectSizes.newLname` applies the configured effect
sizes to those baseline values. Implement these methods for parameters that
use time-varying forcing or vector-control effects; use the existing
bionomics forcing functions where they match the parameter.

For each parameter `x` configured as a port, store its baseline as `x_t`,
its effect size as `es_x`, and its effective value as `x`. Parameters
without ports are stored directly as `x` and are not modified by effect
sizes. The example assumes `p1` has a configured port and that
`F_p1(t, xds_obj, s)` evaluates it; `p2` is a direct parameter without a port.

Inherit the module NULL anchor's `Parameters` section and link the paired
methods reciprocally and to the module. Describe baseline evaluation and
effect-size application separately, keeping stored fields and assignments
in `@note`. For modules without ports, such as stages, describe the actual
no-op behavior rather than claiming that parameters or effects are updated.
Keep dispatch documentation on the shared generics.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Compute the baseline p1 parameter
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_psi
#' @return a numeric vector of length `nHabitats`
#' @export
F_p1 <- function(t, xds_obj, s) {
  UseMethod("F_p1", xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$p1_obj)
}

#' @rdname F_p1
#' @export
F_p1.static <- function(t, xds_obj, s) {
  xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$p1_obj$p1
}

#' @title Mosquito bionomics for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Update baseline parameters and reset effect sizes.
#' @inheritSection newLname Parameters
#' @note Store the evaluated baseline as `p1_t` and reset `es_p1` to 1
#' per habitat at `xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]`. Leave the direct parameter `p2` unchanged.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::LBionomics
#' @seealso [newLname], [LEffectSizes.newLname]
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
LBionomics.newLname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(xds_obj$L_obj[[s]], {
    # Replace these assignments with the appropriate forcing functions.
    xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$p1_t <- F_p1(t, xds_obj, s)
    xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$p2 <- p2
    xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$es_p1 <- rep(1, xds_obj$nHabitats)
    return(xds_obj)
  })
}

#' @title Apply effect sizes for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Apply vector-control effect sizes to baseline parameters.
#' @inheritSection newLname Parameters
#' @note Set `p1 = p1_t * es_p1` at `xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]`.
#' Do not evaluate ports, reset effect sizes, or change the direct parameter `p2`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::LEffectSizes
#' @seealso [newLname], [LBionomics.newLname]
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
LEffectSizes.newLname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(xds_obj$L_obj[[s]], {
    xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$p1 <- p1_t * es_p1
    return(xds_obj)
  })
}
```

## Emergence

`F_emerge.newLname` returns a habitat-level vector of adult emergence,
usually a rate for a continuous-time model or a number for a discrete-time
model. The shared emergence interface aggregates these values to patches
using habitat membership.

Use "Compute adult mosquito emergence for `module` (**L**)" and the short
description below. Inherit the `Emergence` section from the module NULL
anchor for formulas and biological details; keep it consistent with the
implementation. Return "a [numeric] vector of length `nHabitats`" and link
to the module and `ramp.xds::Emergence`. The shared generic documents dispatch
on `xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]`.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Compute adult mosquito emergence for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Return adult female mosquito emergence per habitat.
#' @inheritSection newLname Emergence
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_emerge
#' @seealso [newLname], [ramp.xds::Emergence]
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nHabitats`
#' @export
F_emerge.newLname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(ramp.xds::get_L_vars(y, xds_obj, s), {
    with(xds_obj$L_obj[[s]], {
      # Replace this expression with the model's emergence equation.
      alpha <- rep(0, xds_obj$nHabitats)
      return(alpha)
    })
  })
}
```

## Dynamical parameter accessors

Implement `get_psi`, `get_phi`, `get_xi`, and `get_theta` only when the module
supports these parameter queries. The current methods are provided by `basicL`,
not `stages`. These accessors return stored realized values per habitat;
they do not evaluate ports or apply effect sizes.

Use "Get the parameter for `module` (**L**)" for method titles, replacing
"parameter" with its full name. Describe the stored realized parameter per
habitat, inherit the module NULL anchor's `Parameters` section, and return
"a [numeric] vector of length `nHabitats`". Keep dispatch on
`xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]` in the shared generic documentation. Link to the module
and the corresponding shared parameter changer.

For example, if the module stores a realized maturation rate in `psi`:

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Get the maturation rate for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Return the stored realized maturation rate per habitat.
#' @inheritSection newLname Parameters
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_psi
#' @seealso [newLname], [ramp.xds::change_psi]
#' @return a [numeric] vector of length `nHabitats`
#' @export
get_psi.newLname <- function(xds_obj, s = 1) {
  xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$psi
}
```

## Module object and setup

Use the constructor title "Make a module object for `module` (**L**)".
Describe parameter initialization and `options` overrides. The constructor,
parameter getter, and parameter changer each link to the other two in
`@seealso`; describe any differences in their parameter coverage.

`make_L_obj_newLname` creates the module object and initializes its
parameters. `setup_L_obj.newLname` attaches the object at
`xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]`, sets up initial values, and configures habitat search
weights using the supplied `membership` vector.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Make a module object for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Create a `newLname` module object and initialize its parameters.
#' Inspect parameters with [get_L_pars.newLname] and change supported values
#' with [change_L_pars.newLname]. Values in `options` override parameter arguments.
#' @seealso [get_L_pars.newLname], [change_L_pars.newLname]
#' @param nHabitats the number of habitats in the model
#' @param options a named list of parameter values
#' @return an L module object
#' @export
make_L_obj_newLname <- function(nHabitats, options = list(), p1 = 1, p2 = 1) {
  with(options, {
    L_obj <- list(
      p1 = ramp.xds::checkIt(p1, nHabitats),
      p2 = ramp.xds::checkIt(p2, nHabitats),
      p1_t = ramp.xds::checkIt(p1, nHabitats),
      es_p1 = rep(1, nHabitats),
      p1_obj = structure(list(p1 = ramp.xds::checkIt(p1, nHabitats)),
                         class = "static"),
      nHabitats = nHabitats
    )
    class(L_obj) <- "newLname"
    return(L_obj)
  })
}

#' @title Set up the module object for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Set up a `newLname` module object for the **L** component
#' and the \eqn{s^{th}} vector species.
#' + Create the module object with [make_L_obj_newLname], passing `nHabitats` and `options`.
#' + Set the skill set using [ramp.xds::get_skillset_L].
#' + Set initial values using [ramp.xds::setup_L_inits], passing `options` to override defaults.
#' + Initialize habitat search weights using [ramp.xds::setup_habitat_search_weights.setup].
#' + Return the updated **`xds`** model object.
#' @note The module object is stored at `xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]`.
#' Its classes are `newLname` and `newLname_` followed by `xds_obj$xds`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_L_obj
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
setup_L_obj.newLname <- function(Lname, membership, xds_obj,
                                 options = list(), s = 1) {
  L_obj <- make_L_obj_newLname(xds_obj$nHabitats, options)
  class(L_obj) <- c("newLname", paste0("newLname_", xds_obj$xds))
  xds_obj$L_obj[[s]] <- L_obj
  xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$skill_set <- ramp.xds::get_skillset_L(xds_obj, s)
  xds_obj <- ramp.xds::setup_L_inits(xds_obj, options = options, s = s)
  xds_obj <- ramp.xds::setup_habitat_search_weights(
    "setup", xds_obj, list(membership = membership), s = s
  )
  return(xds_obj)
}
```

## Parameters

The shared `ramp.xds::change_psi`, `ramp.xds::change_phi`,
`ramp.xds::change_xi`, and `ramp.xds::change_theta` helpers are intended for
individual static `basicL` parameters, not arbitrary module-specific fields.
They accept numeric scalars or values of length `nHabitats`, expand scalars
across habitats, and error on invalid types or lengths.
For parameter `x`, they update `xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$x` and, when `x_obj`
is present, also `x_t` and `x_obj$x`. They leave the port class and `es_x`
unchanged, do not evaluate ports or apply effect sizes, and return the
updated model object. They do not dispatch on module or port class and
should not be used to reconfigure dynamic ports.

Their titles retain "Change the parameter (**L**)", using the full parameter
name. Descriptions identify the static `basicL` scope, inherit its
`Parameters` section, and link to the matching getter. Keep storage and
port-field updates in `@note`. New modules should implement their own
`change_L_pars` method for their supported parameters.

Implement `get_L_pars.newLname` to return the module parameters as a named
list, and `change_L_pars.newLname` to update the parameters named in
`options` while leaving other parameters unchanged. Check supplied values
against `xds_obj$nHabitats`; parameter vectors should match the habitat
dimension.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Get parameters for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Return the parameters for the `newLname` module as a named list.
#' @seealso [make_L_obj_newLname], [change_L_pars.newLname]
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_L_pars
#' @return a named [list] of parameter values
#' @export
get_L_pars.newLname <- function(xds_obj, s = 1) {
  with(xds_obj$L_obj[[s]], {
    return(list(p1 = p1, p2 = p2))
  })
}

#' @title Change parameters for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Change parameter values named in `options` for the `newLname`
#' module, leaving other values unchanged.
#' Update the `p1` port and the direct parameter `p2`.
#' The effective `p1` value is set by [LEffectSizes.newLname].
#' Call [ramp.xds::LBionomics] at time zero after the updates,
#' without calling [ramp.xds::LEffectSizes].
#' @seealso [make_L_obj_newLname], [get_L_pars.newLname]
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::change_L_pars
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
change_L_pars.newLname <- function(xds_obj, options = list(), s = 1) {
  nHabitats <- xds_obj$nHabitats
  if ("p1" %in% names(options)) {
    xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$p1_obj$p1 <- ramp.xds::checkIt(options$p1, nHabitats)
  }
  if ("p2" %in% names(options)) {
    xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$p2 <- ramp.xds::checkIt(options$p2, nHabitats)
  }
  y <- ramp.xds::get_inits(xds_obj, flatten = TRUE)
  xds_obj <- ramp.xds::LBionomics(0, y, xds_obj, s)
  return(xds_obj)
}
```

## Initial values

Use the shared `ramp.xds::get_L_inits` function to return stored initial
values for the selected vector species; do not implement a module-specific
getter. It returns the `inits` field directly as a named list, preserves an
empty list (as in `trivialL` after setup), and returns `NULL` if absent.
Getter documentation uses "Get initial values (**L**)", describes returning
stored values, puts storage in `@note`, and links to setup/change functions.

`make_L_inits_newLname` returns defaults as a named list with one value per
habitat for each state. `setup_L_inits.newLname` stores the list on the
module object; users can inspect it with `get_L_inits` and update it with
`change_L_inits.newLname`.

Use the constructor title and description below, preserving any
model-specific explanation. Its return description is "a named [list] of
initial values". The constructor, setup method, and change method each
link to the other two in `@seealso`.
Document numeric scalar expansion to `nHabitats` and the required length
for non-scalar initial values.
For changers, document supported values and special behavior, put storage
explanations in `@note`, and return "an **`xds`** model object". Check
preservation of unspecified values and other species; report implementation
discrepancies separately during documentation alignment.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Make initial values for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Create a named list of initial values for the `newLname` module.
#' Values in `options` override the defaults.
#' @details Initial values must be numeric scalars or have length `nHabitats`.
#' Scalars are expanded to that length.
#' @param nHabitats the number of habitats in the model
#' @param options a named list of initial values
#' @param L the initial value for state `L`
#' @return a named [list] of initial values
#' @seealso [setup_L_inits.newLname], [change_L_inits.newLname]
#' @export
make_L_inits_newLname <- function(nHabitats, options = list(), L = 1) {
  with(options, {
    L <- ramp.xds::checkIt(L, nHabitats)
    return(list(L = L))
  })
}

#' @title Set up initial values for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Set up initial values for the `newLname` module using
#' [make_L_inits_newLname]. Values in `options` override the defaults.
#' @note Initial values are stored at `xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$inits`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_L_inits
#' @seealso [make_L_inits_newLname], [change_L_inits.newLname]
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
setup_L_inits.newLname <- function(xds_obj, options = list(), s = 1) {
  xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$inits <- make_L_inits_newLname(
    xds_obj$nHabitats, options
  )
  return(xds_obj)
}

#' @title Change initial values for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Change initial values named in `options` for the `newLname`
#' module, leaving other values unchanged.
#' @note Stored initial values for this module are at
#' `xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$inits`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::change_L_inits
#' @seealso [make_L_inits_newLname], [setup_L_inits.newLname]
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
change_L_inits.newLname <- function(xds_obj, options = list(), s = 1) {
  with(options, {
    if (!is.null(L)) {
      xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$inits$L <- ramp.xds::checkIt(
        L, xds_obj$nHabitats
      )
    }
  })
  return(xds_obj)
}
```

## State indices

Retrieve stored indices with the shared `ramp.xds::get_L_ix(xds_obj, s = 1)`;
do not implement a module-specific getter. It returns the `ix` field directly:
a named list of variable indices, an empty list if stored, or `NULL` if absent.
Getter documentation uses "Get variable indices (**L**)", describes returning
stored indices for the selected vector species, puts storage in `@note`, and
links to `setup_L_ix`.

`setup_L_ix.newLname` assigns a contiguous range of indices to each state.
Allocate one index per habitat for each habitat-level state, and update
`max_ix` after each range. `get_L_vars.newLname` extracts named states from
the dependent-variable vector `y`.

Use the title and description below, documenting actual block order and
lengths. Put index storage and the updated maximum in `@note`, and return
the model object rather than the index list. Record implementation
exceptions separately during documentation alignment.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Set up variable indices for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Assign consecutive variable indices for the `newLname` module,
#' starting after `xds_obj$max_ix`, and update the maximum index.
#' Allocate the `L_ix` block with length `nHabitats`.
#' @note Indices are stored at `xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$ix`.
#' The maximum index is stored at `xds_obj$max_ix`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_L_ix
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @importFrom utils tail
#' @export
setup_L_ix.newLname <- function(xds_obj, s) {
  L_ix <- seq(from = xds_obj$max_ix + 1, length.out = xds_obj$nHabitats)
  xds_obj$max_ix <- utils::tail(L_ix, 1)
  xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$ix <- list(L_ix = L_ix)
  return(xds_obj)
}

```

## Parsing outputs

After solving, retrieve the saved results with the shared
`ramp.xds::get_L_orbits(xds_obj, s = 1)`; do not implement a module-specific
orbit getter. Its title is "Get orbits (**L**)". It returns a list of
module-specific orbits (trajectories) for **L** for the selected species
from `xds_obj$outputs$orbits$L[[s]]`, with
`time` added from `xds_obj$outputs$time`. It neither parses outputs nor
modifies the model object. Link its documentation to `parse_L_orbits`
and `xds_solve`.

`parse_L_orbits.newLname` extracts each state from the solver output
matrix, using the indices stored on the module object, and returns a named
list. Add derived quantities only when they are useful model outputs.

This method processes trajectories after solving. Document derived quantities
and index storage in its Roxygen block, and use "a [list]" for returns.
It returns results without modifying the model object; the output-processing
pipeline stores them at `xds_obj$outputs$orbits$L[[s]]`.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Parse outputs for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Extract the model state outputs for the `newLname` module
#' from `outputs` and return them by name in a list.
#' @note Variable indices are stored at `xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$ix`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::parse_L_orbits
#' @return a [list]
#' @export
parse_L_orbits.newLname <- function(outputs, xds_obj, s) {
  with(xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$ix, {
    L <- outputs[, L_ix]
    return(list(L = L))
  })
}
```

## Checks and skill set

Setup stores the capabilities and compatibilities returned by
`get_skillset_L.newLname` on the module object. Adapt the flags to the
implemented solver pathways; the example advertises continuous-time
support only. The check method below performs no checks. Add explicit
checks when the module requires them, and describe those checks accurately.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Check `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Return the model unchanged; no checks are implemented in this template.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::check_L
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
check_L.newLname <- function(xds_obj, s) {
  return(xds_obj)
}

#' @title Get the skill set for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Return the capabilities and compatibilities of the `newLname` module as a list.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_skillset_L
#' @return the **L** module skill set, as a list
#' @export
get_skillset_L.newLname <- function(xds_obj, s) {
  list(dts = FALSE, xde = TRUE, delay = FALSE)
}
```

## Optional methods

`steady_state_L.newLname` is optional when a steady-state calculation is
available. It receives habitat-level daily egg input `eta` and returns a
named list of steady-state values. Use "Compute steady states for `module`
(**L**)" for method titles, describe the supported equation system, and
name the returned states. The generic dispatches on `xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]`.
To support both differential-equation and discrete-time calculations, follow
basicL's second-stage dispatch on `xds_obj$xds`; do not assume every module
implements both. Return values are not stored on the model object. The shared
`get_L_orbits`, `xds_plot_L`, and `xds_lines_L` functions provide access
to and visualization of parsed model output; a module-specific plotting
method is not required.

## The `basicL` reference model

The `basicL` module in `ramp.xds` is an example of a habitat-level model.
It tracks larval density \(L\) and implements

\[
\frac{dL}{dt}
= \eta - \left(\psi e^{-\xi L} + \phi + \theta L\right)L,
\qquad
\alpha = \psi e^{-\xi L}L.
\]

Its states and parameters each have one value per habitat. Consult
`aquatic-L-basicL.R` in the `ramp.xds` source for a complete implementation
of its setup, parameter, dynamics, initial-value, emergence, and output
methods.
